title: Homological first-quadrant double complex of modules and its morphisms
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. A *(homological, first-quadrant) double complex of $R$-modules* $A=(A_{p,q},d,\delta)_{p,q\ge0}$ consists of $R$-modules $A_{p,q}$ for $p,q\ge0$ and $R$-linear maps $d_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to A_{p-1,q}$ ($p\ge1$) and $\delta_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to A_{p,q-1}$ ($q\ge1$) such that $d_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}=0$ ($p\ge2$; the rows are complexes), $\delta_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}=0$ ($q\ge2$; the columns are complexes) and $\delta_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}=d_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}$ ($p,q\ge1$; all squares commute). By convention $A_{p,q}=0$ if $p<0$ or $q<0$, and $d_{0,q}$, $\delta_{p,0}$ and every map into or out of a zero module are $0$; with this convention the three identities hold for all $p,q$. A *morphism* $\Phi:A\to B$ of double complexes of $R$-modules is a family of $R$-linear maps $\Phi_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to B_{p,q}$ ($p,q\ge0$) with $d_{p,q}\circ\Phi_{p,q}=\Phi_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}$ and $\delta_{p,q}\circ\Phi_{p,q}=\Phi_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}$ whenever defined; morphisms compose componentwise, $(\Psi\circ\Phi)_{p,q}=\Psi_{p,q}\circ\Phi_{p,q}$, and the identity of $A$ is $(\mathrm{id}_{A_{p,q}})_{p,q}$.
